messages.author: 06c72fc2e70ccfe4
messages.subject: values along vector between timepoints
parts:
Hi all,
I have landmark data from a population sampled in several years. For each combination of two consecutive samples, I would like to get scores for each individual along the vector joining the two samples (similar to PC scores) so that I can measure evolutionary rates along this vector in haldanes. This seems fairly simple but I couldn't find a way to do this in previous posts or the documentation for geomorph or RRPP, so apologies if this has already been asked.

thanks
Grant

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] values along vector between timepoints
parts:
Grant,

If your PC scores are arranged as 1:n, 1:n for individual research subjects, then you can do something like this:

PC.scores <- myPCA$x
ind.vectors <- PC.scores[1:n, ] - PC.scores[((n+1):2*n), ]

If your scores are arranged as 1,1, 2, 2, …, n, n, then something like this might work:

first <- seq(1, 2*n -1, 2)
second <- seq(2, 2*n, 2)
ind.vectors <- PC.scores[first, ] - PC.scores[second, ]

Each of the rows in ind.vectors are changes in PC scores from one time to the next.  Note that I am answering your question about how to get “scores”.  I assume you know how to turn these into Haldanes.

Best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] values along vector between timepoints
parts:
Thanks very much, Mike. I am not quite following what you mean by how my PC scores are arranged, but they are in a matrix with rows as individuals and each PC as a column (as in the output of plotTangentSpace()$pc.scores). Assuming that is the first scenario above, this term PC.scores[((n+1):2*n), ] goes beyond the dimensions of the matrix (e.g. for a 80x79 matrix it tries to refer to rows numbering in the thousands when n=79). 

I should also clarify that for each sample, I have multiple individuals, so I am looking for scores along a vector running between two groups.

thanks again
Grant

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] values along vector between timepoints
parts:
I was assuming you had PC scores for n subjects and 2 time periods, so that you have 2*n rows.  If you have two groups, maybe you first find each group mean vector at each time and subtract the time 1 vector from the time 2 vector, for each group.  The concept is the same but you would have to obtain those vectors first.

Mike
